blocks.title: Compassion fatigue and caregiver load
overview: Healthcare runs on relationships: with patients, with families and with each other. When the pressure stays high for months at a time, people keep caring and start carrying more than anyone can hold. Hard conversations get put off, trust on the team thins, and good people burn out.

Drawing on his years as a therapist and his research with people living with dementia, Stephen gives care teams a practical way to stay compassionate without absorbing everything that comes through the door.
blocks.footnote: The National Academy of Medicine's 2019 report on clinician burnout traces much of that load to how care work is organized.
carried: The conversation nobody wants to have
Being the calm one, every time
The shift that doesn't end at the door

kept.note: This one is for leaders to lift.

outcomes: Recognize caregiver load before it turns into burnout
Hold difficult conversations with patients, families and colleagues
Keep compassion and hold a boundary in the same moment
Rebuild trust on a team that is under pressure
Stay connected to the people beside them, and to why they came into care
